meta.description: In development, not released: a stable C interface to the shared core for C, C++, Unity and Unreal. Written and tested on a feature branch, not merged.

heading: C ABI (in development, not released).
lede: In development, not released: a stable C interface to the shared Rust core for C, C++, Unity and Unreal, with a header-only C++17 wrapper. It is written and tested on a feature branch and not merged, so there is nothing to install yet. This page summarises ABI version 1.2.0 as described in that branch's README and header.
source: bindings/c/README.md and bindings/c/include/{pkg}.h on branch feature/c-abi (commit 9b69b20, ABI 1.2.0, not yet on main); engine SDK status from branch feature/engine-sdks (commit 5db14b2).

sections.heading: Rules
body: Every call returns an nf_status (NF_OK is 0) and sets a per-thread nf_last_error() on failure. Text and bytes come back in an nf_buf that you release with nf_buf_free; it is always NUL-terminated. Each handle has one constructor and one nf_*_free. Nothing panics across the boundary.

The library is compatible with the header when the major part of nf_abi_version() equals NF_ABI_VERSION_MAJOR and its minor part is at least NF_ABI_VERSION_MINOR. A breaking change bumps the major version.

sections.heading: What is exposed (ABI 1.2)
body: The contract of every function is written in the comments of the C header.
Source: bindings/c/README.md, "What is exposed (ABI 1.2)", and include/{pkg}.h (feature/c-abi, 9b69b20).

items.heading: Version, errors, memory
items.body: nf_abi_version, nf_core_version, nf_status_name, nf_last_error, nf_last_error_detail, nf_buf_free, dtype helpers.

items.heading: Hashing spec v1 and v2
items.body: Canonical JSON, number formatting, blob, pipeline-version, chunk and provenance-batch IDs, chain verification, and the spec v2 hashes.

items.heading: Signature verification
items.body: Ed25519 checks of stream chunks, device tokens, provenance-batch signatures, anchors and certificates.

items.heading: Local recordings
items.body: Read-only: open, channel names and units, raw samples, physical values in double precision, timestamps. One read returns at most 1 GiB (2^30 bytes) of stored data; a larger range is rejected before anything is allocated.

items.heading: Chunk cache
items.body: Read-only, hash-verified access to cached chunks.

items.heading: Provenance recorder
items.body: Record, read the chain head, list pending batches, mark them synced.

items.heading: Streaming
items.body: Device keys and tokens, the write-ahead buffer, the stream writer and the sender. Since ABI 1.2, nf_wal_open needs a persistent key (from an OS keystore, or a DPAPI-sealed file on Windows); nf_wal_open_ephemeral, with a key that dies with the process, is for tests only.

items.heading: API client
items.body: Base-URL checks, requests and responses over a caller-supplied HTTP stack.

sections.heading: Bring your own network stack
body: Transports (gRPC for ingest, HTTP for the API) and token stores are supplied by the caller as C callback tables (nf_ingest_transport, nf_http_transport, nf_token_source), so each engine uses its own network stack.

Not exposed, on purpose: anything that sends data or instructions to acquisition hardware, writing recordings or cache entries, raw signing and key export, raw write-ahead-log access, and the hashing-spec payload builders.

sections.heading: Libraries and tests
body: Builds produce a shared and a static library: a DLL with its import library and a static .lib with MSVC, a .so or .dylib and a static .a on Linux and macOS.

Rust tests recompute every frozen hashing test vector through the exported functions and cover NULL and error paths, recordings, the cache, provenance, streaming against a fake ingest server and the API client against a fake HTTP stack. A C test repeats the vectors, error paths, NULL safety and memory round-trips, and a C++ test covers the wrapper.

sections.heading: Pending: ABI 1.2.1
body: Further hardening is planned for ABI 1.2.1 and is not in 1.2.0: a stricter transport contract and caps on reply sizes (the engine transport code already refers to a 64 MiB reply ceiling of 1.2.1).

sections.heading: Unity and Unreal SDKs
body: The engine SDKs are built on this C ABI (version 1.2). Recording reads are split into native calls of at most 64 MiB, under the 1 GiB cap, and opening the write-ahead buffer requires a persistent key. Neither SDK has a device-control or stimulation API.

items.heading: Unity (C# package)
items.body: In development, not released. The C# code is written against C ABI 1.2 but has not been compiled or run yet; its test suite is written but not run.

items.heading: Unreal (plugin)
items.body: In development, not released. Its engine-free C++ core is compiled with MSVC and unit-tested; the Unreal module itself is written but not yet compiled in the editor.
